questions.q: Two towns have local solar times that differ by 1 hour 20 minutes. What is the difference in longitude between them?
questions.explanation: A time difference of 1 hour 20 minutes is 80 minutes. Since 4 minutes of time corresponds to 1° of longitude, the longitude difference is 80 ÷ 4 = 20°. The value 40° would come from using 2 minutes per degree instead of 4 minutes.

questions.q: A telephone call is made from Lagos (GMT+1) at 23:30 on Friday to Beijing (GMT+8). What is the local time in Beijing when the call is received?
questions.explanation: Lagos is 1 hour ahead of GMT, so 23:30 in Lagos is 22:30 GMT on Friday. Beijing is 8 hours ahead of GMT, so the time there is 22:30 + 8 hours = 06:30 on Saturday. The value 07:30 arises from adding 8 hours directly to Lagos time without first converting to GMT.

questions.q: The steep bank cut on the outside of a river meander is formed mainly by which process?
options: wind abrasion along the valley floor
deposition of coarse sand on the inner bend
vertical erosion of the river bed
questions.explanation: On the outer bend, water flows fastest and erodes sideways into the bank, producing a steep river cliff. The inner bend receives slower water where deposition builds a gentle slip-off slope. Vertical erosion deepens the channel but does not specifically create the steep outer bank.

questions.q: A waterfall in a river course gradually retreats upstream mainly because
options: salt weathering by sea spray weakens the gorge sides
alluvium is deposited at the foot of the fall, raising the river bed
lateral erosion cuts the valley sides far downstream of the fall
hydraulic action and abrasion deepen the plunge pool, undercutting the resistant cap rock
questions.explanation: Turbulent water and rock fragments enlarge the plunge pool beneath the fall, removing support from the resistant cap rock, which later collapses and moves the fall upstream. Deposition at the foot of the fall would tend to protect the base rather than cause upstream retreat. Sea spray is a coastal process and does not explain waterfall retreat in a river gorge.

questions.q: Caves and underground channels in limestone regions form mainly through
options: carbonation, as weakly acidic water dissolves calcium carbonate
hydrolysis, as water attacks feldspar in granite
frost shattering, as water freezes and expands in rock cracks
oxidation, as oxygen combines with iron minerals in sandstone
questions.explanation: Rainwater containing dissolved carbon dioxide forms a weak acid that dissolves calcium carbonate in limestone, widening joints into caves and underground channels. Hydrolysis and oxidation affect other minerals and rock types, while frost shattering is a mechanical process that does not dissolve limestone.

questions.q: A supermarket chain wants one large store to serve several towns in Ogun State. According to central place theory, which site is most suitable?
options: a remote hamlet where land is cheapest but few customers pass
a large, centrally located town with good roads to the surrounding towns
a roadside settlement at the edge of the area with the lowest rents
a small village at the exact midpoint of the towns, even though roads are poor
questions.explanation: Central place theory places higher-order services in accessible central settlements with enough population to support them. A geometric midpoint with poor roads is less accessible and may not attract enough customers. Cheap land in remote or peripheral places does not compensate for low demand and poor accessibility.

questions.q: The Mambilla Plateau, known for its cool climate and tea cultivation, is found in which state?
questions.explanation: The Mambilla Plateau lies in Taraba State, near Nigeria's border with Cameroon, and its high altitude gives it a relatively cool climate. Plateau State and Adamawa are nearby or similarly named areas, while the well-known cool highland in Cross River is the Obudu Plateau.

questions.q: Which factor best explains why the rainy season lasts longer in Port Harcourt than in Sokoto?
options: Port Harcourt is nearer the coast, so moisture-bearing south-west monsoon winds persist there for more months
Port Harcourt is at a higher altitude, which increases rainfall
Sokoto is closer to the equator and therefore receives less rain
Sokoto lies under the maritime air mass throughout the year
questions.explanation: Port Harcourt is close to the Atlantic coast and receives moist south-west monsoon air for a longer part of the year. The rain-bearing zone shifts north with the ITCZ, giving Sokoto a shorter wet season. Sokoto is farther north, not closer to the equator, and it is not dominated by maritime air throughout the year.

questions.q: The siting of the Ajaokuta steel complex in Kogi State was influenced mainly by its proximity to
options: crude oil in the Niger Delta
tin and columbite deposits on the Jos Plateau
questions.explanation: The Ajaokuta steel complex is located relatively near the Itakpe iron ore deposits, which provide the essential raw material for steel-making. Coal at Enugu and tin-columbite on the Jos Plateau are important minerals but are not the main locational attraction for Ajaokuta steel. Crude oil in the Niger Delta is unrelated to steel production.

questions.q: On a topographic map with scale 1:50,000, two points on a slope are 4 cm apart on the map. If the difference in height between the points is 100 m, what is the average gradient of the slope?
questions.explanation: Horizontal ground distance = 4 cm × 50,000 = 200,000 cm = 2,000 m. Average gradient = vertical rise ÷ horizontal distance = 100 m ÷ 2,000 m = 1/20, that is 1 in 20. A value of 1 in 50 would arise if the vertical difference were taken as 40 m, which it is not.

questions.q: On a map, the distance between Bida and a nearby village is 7 cm, while the actual straight-line distance is 14 km. What is the scale of the map?
questions.explanation: Convert the ground distance to centimetres: 14 km = 1,400,000 cm. Map scale = map distance ÷ ground distance = 7 cm ÷ 1,400,000 cm = 1/200,000, so the scale is 1:200,000. Treating 14 km as 14 cm would give a much smaller denominator and is incorrect.

questions.q: A river on a map flows from north to south. The contour V-shapes crossed by the river point towards which direction?
questions.explanation: Contour lines form V-shapes that point upstream, opposite to the direction of river flow. Since the river flows southwards, upstream is north, so the V-shapes point north.

questions.q: A fruit-juice factory is established close to orange orchards in Benue State. Which factor best explains this location decision?
options: Government policy requires all fruit-processing firms in Nigeria to be sited in Benue State.
The area has the cool highland climate needed to preserve bottled juice during processing.
The fruit is bulky and perishable, so processing near the orchards reduces transport cost and spoilage.
The finished juice is heavier and bulkier than the fruit, so production must be near consumers.
questions.explanation: Fruit for juice processing is bulky and spoils quickly, so locating the factory near orchards lowers transport and storage losses. The finished juice can then be distributed more cheaply after the bulky waste has been removed.

questions.q: Which Nigerian mineral resource is a white clay used in the manufacture of pottery and ceramic wares?
questions.explanation: Kaolin is a fine white clay used to make pottery and ceramic wares because it can be moulded and fired. Cassiterite is a tin ore, gypsum is used in plaster and cement, and bitumen is mainly used for road surfacing.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: Why do places near the Equator, such as Ibadan, experience almost equal length of day and night throughout the year?
options: The circle of illumination always divides the Equator into two equal parts.
The Moon's gravity equalizes daylight and darkness near the Equator.
The Equator receives direct rays of the Sun throughout the year.
The Earth rotates faster near the Equator than near the poles.
questions.explanation: The circle of illumination always cuts the Equator into two equal halves, so places on the Equator have about 12 hours of daylight and 12 hours of darkness throughout the year. Direct sunlight near the Equator explains high temperatures rather than equal day and night.

questions.q: A farmer in Kano wants to supply 40 kg of nitrogen per hectare using urea fertilizer containing 46% N. How many kilograms of urea should be applied per hectare?
questions.explanation: The mass of urea needed is 40 ÷ 0.46 = 86.96 kg, which is approximately 87 kg. Applying 40 kg of urea would supply only about 18.4 kg of nitrogen, while 46 kg of urea would supply about 21.2 kg.

questions.q: A farmer in Minna wants to improve soil nitrogen by including a leguminous crop in rotation. Which crop is most suitable?
questions.explanation: Cowpea is a legume that can form root nodules with Rhizobium bacteria, which fix atmospheric nitrogen and add it to the soil. Maize, cassava and sorghum are non-legumes and generally remove nutrients from the soil rather than adding nitrogen.

questions.q: A farmer in Ogun State constructs contour bunds across a gently sloping field. The main purpose is to
options: prevent insect pests from reaching the crops
increase soil pH and neutralise acidity
slow down runoff and reduce soil erosion
questions.explanation: Contour bunds follow the slope’s contour and check the speed of surface runoff, allowing more water to infiltrate and reducing erosion. They do not directly correct soil acidity, create ponds for fish farming, or stop insect pests.

questions.q: A soil sample from Abakaliki feels sticky and smooth when wet and forms a long flexible ribbon when squeezed between the fingers. Which texture class is it most likely to be?
questions.explanation: Clay has a high proportion of very fine particles, making it sticky, smooth and able to form a long ribbon. Sandy loam and loamy sand feel gritty and do not ribbon strongly, while silt loam is smooth but has weaker cohesion.

questions.q: Trees with large buttress roots and broad crowns are most characteristic of which vegetation zone in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Buttress roots support tall trees in the moist, multi-storey lowland rainforest, where broad crowns help capture sunlight. Sudan savanna has scattered shorter trees, mangrove swamp has salt-tolerant aerial roots, and montane grassland is dominated by grasses.

questions.q: A local government area in Nasarawa State has a mid-year population of 250,000 and records 7,500 live births in one year. What is its crude birth rate per 1,000 people?
questions.explanation: Crude birth rate = (7,500 ÷ 250,000) × 1,000 = 30 live births per 1,000 people. The result is not 300, which would require 75,000 births for this population.

questions.q: A state has a population of 4.2 million and an area of 28,000 km². What is its population density to the nearest whole number?
questions.explanation: Population density = 4,200,000 ÷ 28,000 = 150 persons per km². A decimal-place error can give 1,500 persons per km², but that would require an area ten times smaller.

questions.q: A rain gauge with a collecting area of 400 cm² records 24 mm of rainfall. What volume of water was collected?
questions.explanation: 24 mm equals 2.4 cm. Volume = collecting area × depth = 400 cm² × 2.4 cm = 960 cm³, which is 0.96 litre. Multiplying by 24 instead of 2.4 gives the too-large value 9,600 cm³.

questions.q: A hiker ascends from a valley at 500 m, where the temperature is 30.0°C, to a peak at 2,500 m. If the average lapse rate is 6.5°C per 1,000 m, what is the expected temperature at the peak?
questions.explanation: The height difference is 2,500 − 500 = 2,000 m, which is 2 km. The temperature drop is 6.5 × 2 = 13.0°C, so the peak temperature is 30.0 − 13.0 = 17.0°C.

questions.q: During a clear day at a coastal town in Lagos, the wind commonly blows from the sea towards the land because
options: the sea heats faster, creating lower pressure over the sea
both land and sea are heated equally, so pressure remains the same
the land cools faster than the sea, causing air to sink over the land
the land heats faster, creating lower pressure over land than over the sea
questions.explanation: During the day, land warms faster than the sea, so air over the land rises and pressure becomes lower there. Air then moves from the relatively higher-pressure sea towards the land as a sea breeze. If the sea were warmer, the pressure pattern and wind direction would reverse.

questions.q: Which factor was most important in the growth of Kano as a centre of long-distance trade in pre-colonial West Africa?
options: Its position on trans-Saharan trade routes
Its equatorial climate favouring rubber plantations
Its deep-water harbour on the Atlantic coast
Its large deposits of coal and iron ore
questions.explanation: Kano grew as a major commercial centre because it lay on the trans-Saharan routes linking West Africa with North Africa. Its inland location, not a coastal harbour, helped it serve as a meeting point for caravans and local markets.

questions.q: A trader in Kano hires lorries to move 240 bags of rice to Ibadan. Each lorry carries 30 bags and charges ₦18,000 per trip. If every lorry makes one trip, what is the total transport cost?
questions.explanation: The number of trips needed is 240 ÷ 30 = 8. The total cost is therefore 8 × ₦18,000 = ₦144,000. Using fewer trips such as 4 or 6 gives the tempting wrong amounts.

questions.q: Which item is classified as an invisible export in Nigeria's external trade?
options: Timber sold to a buyer in Abidjan
Insurance services sold by a Lagos company to a Ghanaian firm
questions.explanation: Invisible exports are services sold to other countries, and insurance services fall into this category. Cocoa, crude oil and timber are tangible goods, so they are visible exports.

questions.q: Which practice best helps to maintain soil fertility in a savanna area without depending mainly on artificial fertilizer?
options: Rotating cereals with legumes and allowing short fallow periods
Increasing the number of grazing animals on the same land
Setting fire to crop residues after every harvest
Growing the same cereal crop on the land every year
questions.explanation: Legumes add nitrogen to the soil, and fallow periods allow natural recovery of fertility. Continuous cereal cropping, burning residues and overgrazing tend to reduce organic matter and increase soil deterioration.

questions.q: A ship sails along longitude 40°W from latitude 30°N to latitude 40°S. Through what total angular distance of latitude does it travel?
questions.explanation: From 30°N to the equator is 30°, and from the equator to 40°S is another 40°. The total angular distance is 30° + 40° = 70°.

questions.q: Why do places near the equator generally have small annual temperature ranges compared with places in high latitudes?
options: The sun is high in the sky throughout the year, so incoming solar energy varies little
They have longer nights than days throughout the year
They are farther from the sun during most of the year
They receive direct sunlight only during the summer solstice
questions.explanation: Near the equator the sun remains high in the sky through the year, and day length is nearly constant, so seasonal heating differences are small. High-latitude areas experience much greater seasonal changes in sun angle and daylight duration.

questions.q: Which process is chiefly responsible for the formation of a river delta at the mouth of a large river?
options: Headward erosion at the source of the river
Vertical erosion of the river bed by eddies
Deposition of sediment where the river's velocity falls on entering standing water
Solution of limestone by underground water
questions.explanation: At a river mouth, the current slows as it enters standing water, causing the load to be deposited. Repeated deposition builds a delta, often with distributaries spreading across it.

questions.q: A settlement that grows mainly at the first point where a road can cross a river is best described as a:
questions.explanation: A bridging-point settlement grows where a river crossing attracts traffic, traders and services. Mining, fishing and defensive sites depend mainly on other factors such as minerals, water or security.

questions.q: Which Nigerian town is an important inland river port on the River Niger?
questions.explanation: Baro is an inland river port on the River Niger in Niger State. Jos, Ogbomoso and Ilesa are not inland ports on the Niger.

questions.q: On a map with scale 1:200,000, the straight-line distance between two villages measures 12.5 cm. What is the actual straight-line distance between the villages?
questions.explanation: The scale 1:200,000 means that 1 cm on the map represents 2 km on the ground. Therefore 12.5 cm represents 12.5 × 2 km = 25 km.

questions.q: On a map with scale 1:100,000, a rectangular game reserve measures 9 cm by 6 cm. What is the actual area of the game reserve?
questions.explanation: At 1:100,000, 1 cm on the map represents 1 km on the ground, so the sides are 9 km and 6 km. The actual area is 9 km × 6 km = 54 km².

questions.q: On a map whose grid north points to the top, a clinic is 4 cm due east and 3 cm due north of a school. Starting from the school, what is the bearing of the clinic?
questions.explanation: The clinic is 3 cm north and 4 cm east of the school, so the direction is east of north. The angle from north satisfies tan θ = 4/3, giving θ ≈ 53°, hence the bearing is 053°.

questions.q: The location of the cement factory at Nkalagu is best explained by its proximity to:
questions.explanation: Cement manufacture uses limestone as its main bulky raw material, so the Nkalagu plant is located near limestone deposits to reduce transport costs. Oil fields, seaports and cocoa plantations do not directly supply the main raw material for cement.

questions.q: A pupil collecting rocks near Lokoja finds a rock containing well-preserved shells. The rock is most likely
questions.explanation: Fossils are best preserved in sedimentary rocks, especially limestone formed from accumulated shelly remains. Granite and basalt are igneous rocks, while marble is metamorphosed limestone and its original fossils are usually destroyed.

questions.q: A mining community on the Jos Plateau extracts a dark, heavy ore that is the chief source of tin. The ore is
questions.explanation: Cassiterite is the main ore of tin and has long been mined on the Jos Plateau. Bauxite is an aluminium ore, galena is a lead ore, and columbite is an ore of niobium and tantalum.
